title: Khalwa, the retreat
hookLine: Sufis make solitary retreats, emptying a room of company to fill it with remembrance

lines: HOME FOR FOOD, THEN OUT AGAIN.
cards: Before the revelation came, a hadith says, solitude was made dear to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. He would go out to a cave called Hira and stay there for a number of nights, worshiping. He took food with him.
When it ran out he came home to his wife Khadija, took more, and went out again. It was there in the cave, the same account says, that the truth came to him.
The hadith's word for that solitude shares its root with today's word, and Sufis look to those nights when they speak of it.

teach.b: Khalwa means seclusion: being alone, emptied of company. In Sufi practice it names a retreat. A person goes into a small room or cell, alone, for a set time, and gives it to remembrance and prayer.
Talk is cut back, food is kept simple, the hours belong to God. And a person doesn't go in on their own say-so.

teach.h: A ROOM, AND A TEACHER'S PERMISSION.
teach.b: They enter with a teacher's permission and under the teacher's eye, because what rises in long silence can be hard to meet alone.

Sufi tradition speaks of a retreat of forty days, and connects it with a forty the Qur'an gives: Moses was appointed thirty nights with his Lord, ten more were added, and the time was completed at forty nights.
Here's the paradox inside the word.

teach.h: EMPTY OF PEOPLE, FULL OF REMEMBRANCE.
teach.b: Khalwa empties a room of people so it can be full of something else. Sufi teachers describe the point not as the being alone, but as what the aloneness makes room for: remembrance without interruption.
Now set it beside yesterday's phrase, solitude in the crowd. The two can sound like rivals: one leaves the market, one stays in it. But Sufi teachers have held both, and some ask for both in turn.
The cave and the market belong to one map.

how: In Sufi orders, a khalwa is a solitary retreat, entered with a shaykh's permission, in which a person spends a set period, from days to weeks, in a small room given to remembrance, prayer and silence.

o: a cave where a prophet hid from his enemies
a Sufi retreat, alone, given to remembrance
a fast kept for forty days and nights

p: where solitude was made dear to him

s: it empties a room of people to make room for remembrance without interruption.
in the tradition, a khalwa is entered with a teacher's permission
what rises in long silence can be hard to meet alone, so a teacher guides it.
the Qur'an tells of Moses's appointed time completed at forty nights
thirty nights, with ten more added: forty in all.

games.q: you feel drawn to a Sufi retreat, alone in a small room for days. what's the traditional first step?
o: lock yourself in tonight and see how it goes.
ask a teacher's permission and guidance.
tell your friends you'll be unreachable.
games.why: a khalwa is entered with a teacher's permission and under the teacher's eye, because long silence can stir up more than a person expects.

practice: For these minutes, turn this space into a khalwa: phone face down or in another room, the door closed if there is one, no company but your breath.

If you pray, let a word of remembrance be the only voice in the room; if you don't, let the silence itself keep you company. When a worry, a list or a memory rises, let it pass through the room and leave.

wordCard.voice: Khalwa. Seclusion: the Sufi retreat, a room emptied of company and given to remembrance. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: seclusion, solitude; in Sufism, a solitary retreat for remembrance.

carryVoice: Your line: khalwa. A person goes in for a while, and learns to carry the quiet back out. Until tomorrow.

sources.work: Hadith (beginning of revelation, narrated by Aisha)
